title: Christmas Lights and Toucan Flights
style: Pop, summer pop with a buoyant midtempo bounce; tight programmed drum mix with crisp snare and punchy kick; Australian female vocals in English, high and light in the verses, gritty and strained in the chorus; keyboards, gliding 808, clipped electric guitars and rattling tambourines; Christmas carols instrumental bridges.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Bogotá in December, uncle's place is warm
Coffee with a friend to lock the plans in stone
Tunja lights and cousins, Christmas tours at dawn
Then Guaymaral airstrip, where the little Toucan's born

[Pre-Chorus]
Thomas says the crossing's gonna be a bigger bird
I've seen the photos, yeah, I've seen the word

[Chorus]
But I'm just here for Christmas lights and family time
Surfing waves I shouldn't, sunburn's mine all mine
The kids are making memories, the ocean's running wild
I'm not looking for a love song, just a friend across the miles

[Verse 2]
The villa's still in scaffolding, the pool is ocean-fed
Esteban wants to surf now, Alicia's catching dread
Lucía's watching nervous from the artificial hill
But we're alive and laughing, and the water's cold but still

[Pre-Chorus]
Thomas asks me questions 'bout the gym and jet lag cure
Something in his smile says there's a plan for sure

[Chorus]
But I'm just here for Christmas lights and family time
Surfing waves I shouldn't, sunburn's mine all mine
The kids are making memories, the ocean's running wild
I'm not looking for a love song, just a friend across the miles

[Bridge]
Last night before we leave, he asks about the mile-high
I play dumb, he shrugs and smiles like he can see right through my eyes
The twenty-first is coming, Air Jaguar on the tarmac
Boeing dreams and berths that lie flat

[Final Chorus]
Still I'm just here for Christmas lights and family time
Toucan flights and surfing, sunburn's mine all mine
The kids have got their stories, the ocean's running wild
I'm not looking for a love song
No, I'm not looking for a love song
Just a friend across the miles

[Outro]
Colombian Christmas morning
Tarmac, dawn, and flight
Just a friend across the miles...
